Maximum rating: - Permalink Show parent Reply In reply to Daniel Gonçalves Re: Muzak by Inês Falcato - Thursday, 26 March 2026, 12:49 PM Hello! For this skill I used SignalMIDI to create my Muzak. I don’t really know much about music theory so I wasn’t sure of what to do. My idea was to create something R&B/Trap/Hip-Hop inspired (which, in the end, I don’t think translated that much). It was a very experimental process. I started by thinking about the drums, because I thought that was the thing that would resemble more the vibe I wanted to go for. I created something very simple inspired by those genres using the snare, hat and kick from the standard drum kit. Then, I created a simple and repeating pattern with the electric piano, using some chords I researched. I duplicated those with a warm pad layer to make it sound more full. Then, taking those chords into consideration, I added a bass layer and tried to make it sound good and match that piano and pad pattern. Finally, I worked on the melody through trial and error until I reached something that I thought made sense and wasn’t just repeating the same 4 bars over and over again. I wasn’t sure what instrument to choose for the melody so I tried most of them and ended up choosing the whistle because I thought it was the most “neutral” sounding one, and it also didn’t feel too distracting. Initially, I made the muzak with 16 bars, but it was too long so I reduced it by 4 bars. I also played around with the bpm value because I started with a lower one but came to the conclusion that I wanted the muzak to be a little faster. The final result is in the attachments. Thank you!
